subject: ectotherm shade levels and ERA5 variable name change issue

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: ectotherm shade levels and ERA5 variable name change issue
parts:
Dear NicheMapR users,

I recently pushed a change to NicheMapR on github to allow hourly rather than daily shade vectors to be passed to the ectotherm model. If you are using the latest github version and have code that specifies the shade manually, it may need updating to account for this.

Re the variable name changes in ERA5 that were discussed in an earlier thread, if you do have old downloads (pre Jan 2025) of ERA5, micro_era5 won't work with them because the mcera5 package has been updated to only recognise the new variable names. One workaround is to simply change the variable names in the old era5 files manually with NCO. Here's an example loop in R to do this:

files<-list.files()
files<-files[grep(".nc", x = files)]
for(i in 1:length(files)){
  filenm <- files[i]
cmd<-paste0("ncrename -h -O -v msdwlwrf,avg_sdlwrf ", filenm)
system(cmd)
cmd<-paste0("ncrename -h -O -v msnlwrf,avg_snlwrf ", filenm)
system(cmd)
}

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 2bcecdd9c0443e65
messages.subject: Re: ectotherm shade levels and ERA5 variable name change issue
parts:
Hi all,

A quick update on that second point that Mike brought up: this has now been just addressed, mcera5 now automatically handles either new or old variable names of ERA5 (these variables don't exist in ERA5-land). If you are using an old query of ERA5, please re-install mcera5 and then micro_era5() should work:

devtools::install_github("dklinges9/mcera5")

As users of mcera5 and micro_era5() may have noted, the ECMWF Climate Data Store (CDS) has been undergoing a lot of changes in the past 6 months, and this may continue as they keep ironing out kinks. Please do notify me (by submitting an issue on the mcera5 GitHub) if you face issues pertinent to mcera5, but first make sure you are using the most updated version of mcera5.

Best,
Dave
